example : Read3Step 0 [2] tp1 (.ok tp1) := .ok (by decide)
example : Write3Step 0 [1] tp1 (.ok (write3Eff tp1 [1])) := .ok (by decide)

/-- `endUse` of a local, then a write and a read in that local (expected: `ok`, `ok`; C8): the
local stays usable, its leaves `Uninit`. -/
example : EndUseStep K0 0 c13a (.ok (endUseEff c13a 0)) := .ok (by decide)
example : (endUseEff c13a 0).Usable 0 ∧ (endUseEff c13a 0).I 0 = .uninit := by decide
example : Write3Step 0 [0] (endUseEff c13a 0) (.ok (write3Eff (endUseEff c13a 0) [0])) :=
  .ok (by decide)
example : Read3Step 0 [0] (write3Eff (endUseEff c13a 0) [0])
    (.ok (write3Eff (endUseEff c13a 0) [0])) := .ok (by decide)

/-! ## Witnesses of the questions of pass 4 -/

/-- On every reached state (MM-03.3.1; D1), the base frame is 0 and stays at the bottom of the
stack, `nF` is positive, the static places keep their indices, and frame 0 owns directly exactly
the static elements without owning element: `enterFrame` gives its locals the new frame or a place
as owner (A5), `alloc` and `transfer` only give places, and the exit never pops the last frame
(O7). The places frame 0 owns transitively (`OwnedByFrame`) are those and the storage they own. -/
theorem reachable_base_owns_statics {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3}
    (h : Reachable k statics s) :
    s.F.getLast? = some 0 ∧ 0 < s.nF ∧ statics.length ≤ s.P.length ∧
      ∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place), s.P[q]? = some pl →
        (pl.owner = .frame 0 ↔
          q < statics.length ∧ ((statics.map (·.1))[q]?).bind (·.2.1) = none) := by
  induction h with
  | init hsh =>
    refine ⟨rfl, Nat.zero_lt_one, Nat.le_of_eq (init_len statics).symm, fun q pl hq => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨hql, rfl⟩ := init_P_get hq
    simp only [shapeOwner]
    split
    · rename_i o ho
      exact ⟨fun e => (by cases e), fun ⟨_, h⟩ => (by rw [ho] at h; cases h)⟩
    · rename_i ho
      exact ⟨fun _ => ⟨hql, ho⟩, fun _ => rfl⟩
  | derive _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | split _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | @release s s' a _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    unfold releaseEff; split <;> exact ih
  | @transfer s s' src dst _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    refine ⟨ih.1, ih.2.1, by rw [transfer_len]; exact ih.2.2.1, fun q pl hq => ?_⟩
    rw [transfer_P_get] at hq
    obtain ⟨pl₀, h₀, rfl⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.1 hq
    have e := ih.2.2.2 q pl₀ h₀
    split
    · rename_i hh
      have hp : pl₀.owner ≠ .frame 0 := fun e' => by rw [e'] at hh; exact hh
      simp only [reduceCtorEq, false_iff]
      exact fun h' => hp (e.2 h')
    · exact e
  | depend _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | @enter s s' ps ls _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4⟩ := ih
    refine ⟨?_, by simp [enterEff], ?_, fun q pl hq => ?_⟩
    · show (s.nF :: s.F).getLast? = some 0
      cases hF : s.F with
      | nil => rw [hF] at h1; cases h1
      | cons a l => rw [hF] at h1; rw [List.getLast?_cons_cons]; exact h1
    · show statics.length ≤ (enterP s ls).length
      rw [enterP_len]; omega
    · rcases enterP_get (show (enterP s ls)[q]? = some pl from hq) with ⟨-, hq'⟩ | ⟨hge, i, -, -, rfl⟩
      · exact h4 q pl hq'
      · have : ¬ q < statics.length := by omega
        simp only [this, false_and, iff_false]
        simp only [localOwner]; split
        · simp
        · intro e; injection e with e; omega
  | @exit s s' _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    unfold exitEff
    unfold ExitPre at hpre
    split
    · rename_i f F₀ hF
      rw [hF] at hpre
      obtain ⟨hne, -⟩ := hpre
      refine ⟨?_, ih.2.1, ih.2.2⟩
      have := ih.1; rw [hF] at this
      cases F₀ with
      | nil => exact absurd rfl hne
      | cons g F₁ => rw [List.getLast?_cons_cons] at this; exact this
    · exact ih
  | read _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | write _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | writeShared _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | pin _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | unpin _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | endUse _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | free _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | @alloc s s' pr ow ls _ h ih =>
    cases h with
    | ok _ _ =>
      obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3, h4⟩ := ih
      refine ⟨h1, h2, ?_, fun q pl hq => ?_⟩
      · show statics.length ≤ (allocP s ow ls).length
        rw [allocP_len]; omega
      · rcases shapeP_get (show (shapeP s.P (.place ow) ls)[q]? = some pl from hq) with
          ⟨-, hq'⟩ | ⟨hge, i, -, -, rfl⟩
        · exact h4 q pl hq'
        · have : ¬ q < statics.length := by omega
          simp only [this, false_and, iff_false]
          simp only [shapeOwner]; split <;> simp
  | newArena _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; unfold newArenaEff; split <;> exact ih
  | issue _ h ih => cases h with
    | ok _ hst => cases hst; exact ih
  | reset _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; unfold resetAtEff; split <;> exact ih

/-- A static leaf pinned by `K.Pinned` (C5; D1), as a memory-mapped register would be: the
contract `KPS` pins the leaf 0 of the static storage `stPin`, one global with an initialiser. -/
abbrev KPS : K := KT [] [0] [] [] []
def stPin : Statics := [((none, none, 0), true)]
def sp1 : S3 := enterEff (S3.init stPin) [] [(none, none, 0)]

/-- `static_pinned_never_exits` has content on a reached state (C5; D1): `K.Pinned` is not empty,
`StaticPinnedBottom` holds since frame 0 owns the pinned global, and the exit of frame 1 kills its
local, which covers no pinned leaf. -/
theorem staticPinned_reached :
    Reachable KPS stPin sp1 ∧ KPS.Pinned 0 ∧ StaticPinnedBottom KPS sp1 ∧
      ExitStep KPS sp1 (.ok (exitEff sp1)) ∧
      ∀ q, sp1.Usable q → ¬ ({ sp1 with F := [0] } : S3).Usable q →
        ∀ l ∈ footprint sp1.P q, ¬ KPS.Pinned l := by
  have hr : Reachable KPS stPin sp1 := .enter (.init (by decide)) (.ok (by decide))
  have hsp : StaticPinnedBottom KPS sp1 := by
    intro l hl
    have : l = 0 := List.mem_singleton.1 hl
    subst this
    exact ⟨0, by decide, show OwnedByFrame sp1.P 0 0 from .frame (pl := ⟨none, .frame 0, 0⟩)
      (by decide) rfl⟩
  exact ⟨hr, List.mem_singleton_self _, hsp, .ok (by decide),
    static_pinned_never_exits (reachable_access_invariant_underDD (KT_dd [] [0] [] [] []) hr).1 hsp
      (show sp1.F = 1 :: [0] from rfl) (by decide)⟩

/-- Reading the base frame of C5 as the first frame entered does not help: in `c13a`, the local 0
belongs to frame 1, the first frame entered, and stops being usable when frame 1 exits. -/
example : c13a.F = [1, 0] ∧ c13a.Usable 0 ∧ ¬ ({ c13a with F := [0] } : S3).Usable 0 ∧
    0 ∈ footprint c13a.P 0 ∧ OwnedByFrame c13a.P 1 0 :=
  ⟨rfl, by decide, by decide, by decide, .frame (pl := ⟨none, .frame 1, 0⟩) rfl rfl⟩

/-- `alloc` of the empty shape (pass-4 question (e) 2): pass 4 accepted it, with no new place and
no new authority, the state `allocEff (write3Eff n6e [1]) 1 0 []` below. D2 rejects it. -/
example : AllocStep K0 1 0 [] (write3Eff n6e [1]) .reject := .reject (by decide)
example : (allocEff (write3Eff n6e [1]) 1 0 []).P = (write3Eff n6e [1]).P ∧
    (allocEff (write3Eff n6e [1]) 1 0 []).A = (write3Eff n6e [1]).A := by decide

/-! ## New cases of pass 5 -/

/-! ### Static storage (D1) -/

/-- Two globals: 0 with an initialiser (`Init`), 1 without (`Uninit`), owned by frame 0, each with
a root held by frame 0 (D1). -/
def stG : Statics := [((none, none, 0), true), ((none, none, 0), false)]
def g0 : S3 := S3.init stG

/-- A global `Init` read by frame 0 (expected: `ok`); a global `Uninit` read (expected: reject),
written then read (expected: `ok`, `ok`). -/
example : Read3Step 0 [0] g0 (.ok g0) := .ok (by decide)
example : Read3Step 1 [1] g0 .reject := .reject (by decide)
example : Write3Step 1 [1] g0 (.ok (write3Eff g0 [1])) := .ok (by decide)
example : Read3Step 1 [1] (write3Eff g0 [1]) (.ok (write3Eff g0 [1])) := .ok (by decide)

/-- A global written by a callee without parameter (expected: reject): the root of the global is
held by frame 0, which the callee does not exercise (A2). With a `Modify` parameter derived by the
caller (A3), the write is accepted. -/
example : EnterStep [] [] g0 (.ok (enterEff g0 [] [])) := .ok (by decide)
example : Write3Step 0 [0] (enterEff g0 [] []) .reject := .reject (by decide)
def g3 : S3 := enterEff (deriveEff g0 0 0 .modify) [2] []
example : DeriveStep 0 0 .modify g0 (.ok (deriveEff g0 0 0 .modify)) := .ok (by decide)
example : EnterStep [2] [] (deriveEff g0 0 0 .modify) (.ok g3) := .ok (by decide)
example : Write3Step 2 [0] g3 (.ok (write3Eff g3 [0])) := .ok (by decide)
example : Reachable K0 stG g3 :=
  .enter (.derive (.init (by decide)) (.ok (by decide))) (.ok (by decide))

/-- A memory-mapped register as a pinned static (D1): the global 0 is pinned by `K.Pinned`
(`KPS`). The test checks the access discipline only: `transfer` and `endUse` are rejected, reads
and writes allowed by the discipline are accepted. The semantics of a hardware access, read side
effects and external modifications, is outside the kernel and not represented. -/
def mm0 : S3 := S3.init stG
example : TransferStep KPS 0 1 mm0 .reject := .reject (by decide)
example : EndUseStep KPS 0 mm0 .reject := .reject (by decide)

2. **`EffAnchorOK` sans cas permissif.** `EffAnchorOK s x fd` exige que l'ancre effective existe, que son détenteur ait un cadre, que le dépendant en ait un, et que le premier soit le second ou un de ses ancêtres. `NoEscape` (passe 3) admettait par défaut une ancre sans cadre ou un emplacement sans cadre. L'activité de l'ancre effective n'est pas exigée : C1 n'en parle pas, et I3 porte sur l'ancre elle-même.
3. **Clause B8 de `transfer` (C1).** Elle contrôle l'ancre effective quand celle-ci bouge avec la valeur, comme en passe 3, et aussi quand le dépendant bouge : la destination, ou un emplacement que la valeur possède. C'est aussi MM-03.3.6 lu sur l'ancre effective : « Une valeur dépendante ne peut être installée dans une destination dont le cadre survivrait à celui d'une ancre locale dont elle dépend ». La clause découle de `AnchorOrder` de l'état d'arrivée : elle ne rejette que les transferts qui le violeraient. Conséquence : les cas 10 et n9 sont rejetés au `transfer` ((g)).
4. **`NoEscape` gardé dans `DependPre` et dans la clause 6 de `TransferPre` (B7).** C1 ne retire pas ces clauses. Pour une ancre sans origine, l'ancre effective est l'ancre elle-même, et `EffAnchorOK` au même cadre implique `NoEscape` ; pour une ancre dérivée, `NoEscape` ne dit rien.
5. **`NoDangling` (C2), lu à la lettre.** Pour toute autorité active, tout emplacement non utilisable et toute feuille de son empreinte, l'autorité ne couvre pas cette feuille. L'initialisation n'est pas lue.
6. **Hypothèses des préservations.** Chaque préservation d'`AnchorOrder` prend `AnchorOrder s`, et `WF3 s` quand elle en a besoin. verdicts.title: Decision (1) is not forced by WF3: it lets a static belong to another static, and that changes behaviour (static places can die while frame 0 is live)
verdicts.reasoning:
The Lean witnesses are correct: I re-ran owned_static2.lean and owned_static3.lean, and they compile with axioms [propext, Quot.sound]. The conclusion drawn from them does not follow.

(i) D1 fixes the encoding of statics: "`statics` au même encodage que les locaux de `enterFrame`". That encoding includes an owning element. C6 uses the same phrase for `alloc` shapes. Pass-4 decision 12 settled it, and that decision is in force (MM03_v0.1_p4.md, (c) 12): "La composante « élément propriétaire » garde son sens de `enterFrame` : un élément peut être possédé par un élément antérieur ; les autres sont possédés par `owner`. Une racine d'autorité `Modify` par élément racine, sur son empreinte, détenue par le propriétaire de l'élément (A4)." B5 used the same pattern as D1 ("possédée par `owner`, racine d'autorité `Modify` détenue par `owner`"). Pass 4 read it as decision (1) reads D1 now. The D arbitrages answered the pass-4 questions (e)1 and (e)2 and did not overturn (c) 12. Decision (1) is therefore that in-force decision applied to `hd = .frame 0`. A4 settles the holder: "Une racine reste détenue par le propriétaire de son emplacement". C5 already anticipates transitive ownership: "possédé, transitivement, par le cadre de base".

(ii) Option A forbids owning elements in statics. That would restrict the encoding D1 fixes, so it is not a reading the brief leaves open.

(iii) Behaviours (a)-(c) follow from in-force rules that apply equally to locals and allocated shapes (`enterP_eq_shapeP`, `allocP = shapeP`). C8 says "Seuls les emplacements possédés par p deviennent logiquement morts" (case a). A2/A5 cover case b. D1 itself says a callee exercises frame-0 roots "par un paramètre dérivé (A2, A3) ; aucune règle d'accès supplémentaire". In case (c), `StaticPinnedBottom` is by C5 an obligation and a "Hypothèse nommée des seuls théorèmes qui en ont besoin". The module never claims it is invariant: grep shows it is used only as a hypothesis or in witnesses. The reviewer's own witness shows `ExitStep KP2 o3 .reject`, so the pinned leaf never dies.

The only valid point is presentational. The implementer's stated reason ("without this WF3 fails") omits the stronger reason, pass-4 decision 12. That is report wording, not a formalization defect.

verdicts.title: reachable_base_owns_statics only covers direct ownership; step 1's 'frame 0 owns exactly the static places' is false here and the gap is not reported
verdicts.reasoning:
The theorem is not restricted to a subset. It quantifies over every reached state and every place, and states an iff. The owning-element condition is on the right-hand side of that iff, as part of the exact characterization; it is not a hypothesis. The reviewer's proposed restatement (`owner = .frame 0 ↔ q < statics.length`) is also about direct ownership. It differs only because Option A changes which statics are allowed, so this finding depends entirely on finding 1, which is refuted.

Under the in-force reading (pass-4 decision 12), a static with an owning element is the owned storage of the static that owns it. Step 1 asks: "le cadre 0 possède exactement les emplacements statiques et leur stockage possédé". That maps to direct ownership of the statics without an owning element, plus transitive ownership (`OwnedByFrame`) of whatever they currently own. The docstring says exactly this: "The places frame 0 owns transitively (OwnedByFrame) are those and the storage they own". That holds by the definition of OwnedByFrame.

Owned storage follows transfers (A5: "Le transfert d'une valeur transfère la possession de ses emplacements possédés"). The reviewer's witness, where static 2 leaves frame 0, is therefore that owned storage moving, as A5 says it must. Under Option A the same thing happens to storage a static owns through `alloc`. Neither reading lets a step-1 statement say that a static's owned storage stays with frame 0 forever. The docstring makes no false claim, and the statement was not weakened.

verdicts.title: Statics docstring says the flag is per global; the code reads it per leaf, so a non-leaf element's flag is ignored
verdicts.reasoning:
The code does what D1 asks: "plus l'état initial de chaque feuille". The state is given per leaf, and `S3.init` sets `I l` from element l's own flag. Per-leaf states are also allowed by MM-03.3.3 ("Les valeurs composites peuvent être partiellement initialisées"). So there is no semantic error, and the alternative fix (deriving each leaf's state from its global) is not required.

The docstring, however, misdescribes the flag. It says each element comes "with the initial state of its leaves, `true` for a global with an initialiser (`Init`)". For an element that has parts, the flag is ignored, and its leaves take their own flags. I re-ran flag.lean and it compiles: stC = [((none,none,0),true), ((some 0,none,0),false)] gives footprint 0 = [1], I 1 = .uninit, and the read is rejected, even though element 0 is the global flagged 'with an initialiser'. This is a docstring inaccuracy only. The fix is to state that the flag is a leaf's initial state and is unused for non-leaf elements.

verdicts.title: reachable_base_owns_statics only covers direct ownership; step 1's 'frame 0 owns exactly the static places' is false here and the gap is not reported
verdicts.reasoning:
The theorem is not restricted to a subset. It quantifies over every reached state and every place, and states an iff. The owning-element condition is on the right-hand side of that iff, as part of the exact characterization; it is not a hypothesis. The reviewer's proposed restatement (`owner = .frame 0 ↔ q < statics.length`) is also about direct ownership. It differs only because Option A changes which statics are allowed, so this finding depends entirely on finding 1, which is refuted.

Under the in-force reading (pass-4 decision 12), a static with an owning element is the owned storage of the static that owns it. Step 1 asks: "le cadre 0 possède exactement les emplacements statiques et leur stockage possédé". That maps to direct ownership of the statics without an owning element, plus transitive ownership (`OwnedByFrame`) of whatever they currently own. The docstring says exactly this: "The places frame 0 owns transitively (OwnedByFrame) are those and the storage they own". That holds by the definition of OwnedByFrame.

The reviewer's witness, where static 2 leaves frame 0, is therefore that owned storage moving, as A5 says it must. Under Option A the same thing happens to storage a static owns through `alloc`. Neither reading lets a step-1 statement say that a static's owned storage stays with frame 0 forever. The docstring makes no false claim, and the statement was not weakened.

verdicts.title: Statics docstring says the flag is per global; the code reads it per leaf, so a non-leaf element's flag is ignored
verdicts.reasoning:
The code does what D1 asks: "plus l'état initial de chaque feuille". The state is given per leaf, and `S3.init` sets `I l` from element l's own flag. Per-leaf states are also allowed by MM-03.3.3 ("Les valeurs composites peuvent être partiellement initialisées"). So there is no semantic error, and the alternative fix (deriving each leaf's state from its global) is not required.

The docstring, however, misdescribes the flag. It says each element comes "with the initial state of its leaves, `true` for a global with an initialiser (`Init`)". I re-ran flag.lean and it compiles: stC = [((none,none,0),true), ((some 0,none,0),false)] gives footprint 0 = [1], I 1 = .uninit, and the read is rejected, even though element 0 is the global flagged 'with an initialiser'. This is a docstring inaccuracy only. The fix is to state that the flag is a leaf's initial state and is unused for non-leaf elements.
